stem:
In industry, ethanol is made by reacting ethene with steam in the presence of $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$.

reaction 1 $$\text{C}_2\text{H}_4(\text{g}) + \text{H}_2\text{O}(\text{g}) \rightleftharpoons \text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}(\text{g})$$

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Use the bond energy values in Table 4.1 to calculate the enthalpy change, $\Delta H_{\text{r}}$, for reaction 1.

Table 4.1

| bond | bond energy/$\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ |
| :--- | :--- |
| $\text{C-C}$ | 350 |
| $\text{C=C}$ | 610 |
| $\text{C}\equiv\text{C}$ | 840 |
| $\text{C-H}$ | 410 |
| $\text{C-O}$ | 360 |
| $\text{C=O}$ | 740 |
| $\text{O-H}$ | 460 |

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Reaction 1 reaches equilibrium at constant temperature and pressure.

Deduce what effect increasing the pressure will have on the amount of ethanol in the new equilibrium mixture. Use Le Chatelier's principle to explain your answer.

parts.label: (c)
(c)(i)
parts.text: Describe the behaviour of $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$ in step 1 in Fig. 4.1. Explain your answer.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Identify the species that behaves as an electrophile in step 2 in Fig. 4.1. Explain your answer.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
(c)(iv)
parts.text: Describe how a catalyst affects a reaction. Explain your answer.

parts.label: (c)(v)
parts.text: Use Fig. 4.1 and Fig. 4.2 to justify why $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$ is described as a catalyst in reaction 1.

parts.label: (c)(vi)
parts.text:
Propene also reacts with steam. A mixture of organic products is produced.

Explain why propan-2-ol is produced in the higher yield.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
